texts.text: NASA estimated the meteorite was roughly 50 feet (15 meters) in diameter when it entered Earth’s atmosphere, travelling faster than the speed of sound, and exploded into a fireball brighter than the sun. Amateur video show by Russian television depicted a white streak of light like the cloud from a jetliner quickly expanding to a large white ball that eventually sent shock waves throughout the city of Chelyabinsk. None of the existing celestial tracking systems, either Russian or American, detected the meteor until it entered the atmosphere,” Director of the Astronomy Institute of the Russian Academy of Sciences Boris Shustov told the newswire.

texts.text: Monastic clergy wear different headcoverings than married clergy. Married clergy wear either a colored kalimaukion or skufia; monastic clergy wear a black kalimaukion and veil (together known as the klobuk). For monastics, the skufia is reserved for house dress, and the klobuk is worn in church. Russian archbishops have a jewelled cross attached to the front of their klobuks; Russian Metropolitans wear a white klobuk with jewelled cross. Several Orthodox Patriarchs wear a rounded headcovering called a koukoulion.
texts.note: [draft] Russian Orthodox clergy dress is only part of a general Orthodox vestments paragraph; religious dress as 'tradition' is a stretch.

texts.text: Maslenitsa, the Russian week-long festival that marks the end of winter, is all about blini. Families fry stacks of thin pancakes and eat them with sour cream, honey, jam or red caviar. In towns across Russia there are sledging contests, folk games and, on the last day, a straw figure of Lady Winter is burned in a bonfire. The final Sunday is called Forgiveness Sunday.
texts.note: Describes a Russian holiday tradition and food.

lactobacillus bacteria

Lactobacillus Bulgaricus
(shown here in brown)
Credit: Utah State University

The well-known Russian scientist Ilya Metchnikoff - one of the founders of modern immunology - linked the longevity of the Bulgarian people to the consumption of yoghurt. Metchnikoff, at that time a professor at the Pasteur Institute in Paris, produced the notion that the aging process results from the activity of putrefactive (proteolytic) microbes producing toxic substances in the bowels. Proteolytic bacteria such as clostridia, which are part of the normal gut flora, produce toxic substances including phenols, indols and ammonia from the digestion of proteins. According to Metchnikoff these compounds were responsible for what he called "intestinal auto-intoxication", which caused the physical changes associated with old age. It was at that time known that milk fermented with lactic-acid bacteria inhibits the growth of proteolytic bacteria because of the low pH produced by the fermentation of lactose. Metchnikoff had also observed that certain rural populations in Europe, for example in Bulgaria and the Russian Steppes who lived largely on milk fermented by lactic-acid bacteria were exceptionally long lived. Based on these facts, Metchnikoff proposed that consumption of fermented milk would "seed" the intestine with harmless lactic-acid bacteria and decrease the intestinal pH and that this would suppress the growth of proteolytic bacteria.
texts.note: [draft] Russian scientist Metchnikoff, but his work was done at the Pasteur Institute in Paris.

cases.title: News that debunks a narrative

texts.text: Russian officials have claimed that images of dead civilians in Bucha were 'staged' after Russian forces withdrew. Satellite images published by Maxar Technologies, however, show bodies lying in the streets in mid-March 2022, while the town was still under Russian control. UN investigators and journalists later documented unlawful killings there, contradicting the Kremlin's version of events.
texts.note: Fact-check quoting the denial and refuting it.

texts.text: FACT CHECK: Did Ukraine run secret US-funded bioweapons labs? No. The claim, promoted by Russia's defence ministry in March 2022, refers to public-health laboratories that the United States helped upgrade under a programme to secure dangerous pathogens left over from the Soviet era. The World Health Organization and independent experts found no evidence of weapons research.
texts.note: Fact-check attributing a claim to the Russian defence ministry and refuting it.
